title: Invisalign in Markham: Cost, Timeline & What to Expect
seoTitle: Invisalign Markham: Cost, Timeline & What to Expect | Smile Dental Arts Centre
metaDescription: Thinking about Invisalign in Markham? Learn what treatment costs, how long it takes, what the process feels like, and how it compares to traditional braces.
excerpt: Invisalign uses a series of clear, custom-made aligners to gradually straighten teeth without the metal brackets and wires of traditional braces. This guide covers everything Markham patients need to know: cost, timeline, the step-by-step process and what to expect daily.
intro: Invisalign has transformed orthodontic treatment for millions of patients worldwide by replacing metal brackets and wires with a series of clear, removable plastic aligners. For adults and teens in Markham who want a straighter smile without the visibility or dietary restrictions of traditional braces, Invisalign offers a compelling alternative. At Smile Dental Arts Centre, Dr. Neda Kadivar is a certified Invisalign provider with extensive experience treating a wide range of alignment cases — from mild crowding to more complex bite corrections.

This guide answers the questions patients ask most at their first Invisalign consultation: how much does it cost in the Markham area, how long does treatment take, what does wearing the aligners feel like, and how does Invisalign compare to braces? Read through each section before you book so you arrive ready to make a confident decision.

blocks.text: Invisalign treatment begins with digital impressions of your teeth — no messy traditional putty required. Using the iTero scanner at our clinic, we capture a precise 3D model of your current bite. That model is sent to [Invisalign](https://www.invisalign.ca/) where specialist software creates a digital treatment plan showing the projected movement of your teeth at each stage. You can view the before-and-after simulation of your predicted smile before committing to treatment.

A series of custom aligners — typically 20 to 40 sets for a comprehensive case — are then fabricated. Each aligner is worn for one to two weeks before being swapped for the next in the series. The aligners apply gentle, continuous pressure on specific teeth, gradually moving them toward their target positions. Small tooth-coloured attachments bonded to certain teeth help the aligners grip and apply forces in more precise directions — these are barely visible but worth knowing about in advance.

items: Wear aligners 20–22 hours per day — remove only to eat, drink anything other than water, and brush.
Change to the next aligner set every 1–2 weeks as directed by Dr. Kadivar.
Attend check-up appointments every 6–10 weeks to monitor progress and receive the next batch of aligners.
Attachments (small tooth-coloured bumps on certain teeth) improve aligner grip for complex movements.
Retainers are worn after treatment to hold your teeth in their new positions permanently.

blocks.text: Treatment time varies significantly by case complexity. Minor crowding or spacing corrections — the kinds of adjustments that move just a few teeth slightly — may complete in as little as six months with Invisalign Lite (typically 14 aligners or fewer). Comprehensive full-arch treatments addressing significant crowding, spacing, or bite correction typically take 12 to 24 months. The average comprehensive Invisalign case in our Markham clinic is completed in 14 to 18 months.

Compliance is the biggest variable in how long treatment takes. Because aligners are removable, the patient controls whether they are in the mouth for the required 20–22 hours per day. Wearing aligners less than this slows tooth movement and can extend the total treatment time by months. Patients who are highly compliant often complete treatment at or ahead of their initial estimate; inconsistent wearers frequently require additional aligner sets, adding both time and cost.

Invisalign treatment in Markham typically ranges from **$3,000 to $7,500** depending on the product tier selected and the complexity of the case. Invisalign Lite (for mild corrections with fewer than 14 aligners) sits at the lower end; Invisalign Comprehensive (full treatment addressing complex issues) is at the higher end. These ranges reflect the [Ontario Dental Association](https://www.oda.ca/) fee guide benchmarks and the particular demands of each case.

The all-inclusive fee should cover your initial impressions, all aligner sets, attachments, any needed refinements (additional aligner stages if the teeth have not reached their planned positions at the end of the original series), and your first set of retainers. Ask specifically about refinements before signing any treatment agreement — some offices charge extra for these, which is worth knowing upfront. Our Markham clinic includes one refinement cycle within the original fee for comprehensive cases.

Many Ontario dental plans include an orthodontic benefit — commonly between $1,500 and $3,500 as a lifetime maximum — that applies equally to Invisalign and traditional braces. There is typically no penalty for choosing Invisalign over braces from an insurance standpoint; both are recognised orthodontic treatments. If your plan has an orthodontic waiting period, confirm it has been met before beginning treatment.

Patients enrolled in the [Canadian Dental Care Plan](https://www.canada.ca/en/services/benefits/dental/dental-care-plan.html) who meet eligibility requirements may have some orthodontic services covered for children and youth. Adults on the CDCP may have limited orthodontic coverage; check with your benefits coordinator or our administrative team before booking. Financing over 12–36 months is also available at our clinic for the out-of-pocket balance, making monthly payments manageable for most budgets.

sections.heading: What Does Wearing Invisalign Feel Like?

blocks.text: New patients often ask whether Invisalign is painful. The accurate answer is: not painful, but pressure is felt — particularly within the first day or two of switching to a new aligner set. This pressure sensation is the aligners applying force to move teeth and is a sign the treatment is working. It typically fades within 48–72 hours of inserting a new set. Over-the-counter ibuprofen or acetaminophen manages the discomfort easily in the first day or two of each new aligner.

Speech is mildly affected initially — a slight lisp is common in the first week while the tongue adjusts to the aligners. Most patients adapt fully within one to two weeks and speak completely normally. The aligners feel smooth against cheeks and lips, unlike metal braces which commonly cause irritation. Eating and drinking are unaffected because the aligners come out for meals.

Daily routine tip: Keep a case for your aligners in your pocket or bag so you always have somewhere to put them during meals. Wrapping aligners in a napkin at restaurants is the most common cause of accidentally discarding them — it happens more often than you would think.

sections.heading: Invisalign vs. Braces: Which Is Better?

blocks.text: Neither is universally superior — the better option depends on your clinical needs and lifestyle preferences. Invisalign is significantly more discreet, more comfortable against soft tissue, allows unrestricted eating and simplifies oral hygiene (brush and floss normally after removing aligners). Braces work around the clock whether you think about them or not — compliance is controlled — which gives some patients better outcomes if they know their discipline with removable appliances is inconsistent. The detailed comparison is in our article on [Invisalign vs. traditional braces](/blog/invisalign-vs-braces).

Complex bite corrections — significant overbite, underbite, crossbite, or extreme crowding requiring extractions — have historically been managed better with braces, though Invisalign technology has closed this gap considerably over the past decade. At your consultation, Dr. Kadivar will give an honest assessment of whether your specific case can be treated as effectively with Invisalign as with braces, so you can make the choice with full information.

Orthodontic treatment does not end when you reach your final aligner — it transitions into the retention phase. Teeth have a natural tendency to drift back toward their original positions if not held in place, a process called orthodontic relapse. Retainers prevent this. Most patients are given clear retainers similar to Invisalign aligners, worn full-time for the first three to six months after treatment and then only at night indefinitely.

Permanent bonded retainers — a thin wire glued to the backs of the front teeth — are another option, particularly for patients who worry about remembering to wear a removable retainer at night. These are invisible, maintenance-free and highly effective at preventing relapse of the front teeth. A full guide to maintaining results after Invisalign is in our [retainers after Invisalign](/blog/retainers-after-invisalign) article.

sections.heading: Getting Started at Smile Dental Arts Centre in Markham

blocks.text: Your Invisalign journey at Smile Dental Arts Centre begins with a complimentary consultation that includes a digital scan with the iTero element scanner, a review of your case complexity and treatment options, a demonstration of your ClinCheck smile simulation, and a written cost and timeline estimate. There is no obligation to proceed, and you will leave with a clear picture of what Invisalign can achieve for your specific smile.

Dr. Neda Kadivar is a certified Invisalign provider and a member of the [Royal College of Dental Surgeons of Ontario](https://www.rcdso.org/). Our clinic at 3980 14th Ave, Markham, is open Monday through Friday with extended hours and every other Saturday. [Book your Invisalign consultation](/appointments) today.

title: Invisalign vs. Traditional Braces: Pros and Cons
seoTitle: Invisalign vs. Traditional Braces: Pros and Cons | Smile Dental Arts Centre Markham
metaDescription: Invisalign or braces? Compare comfort, aesthetics, cost, treatment time and suitability for different cases so you can make the right choice in Markham.
excerpt: Invisalign and traditional braces both straighten teeth effectively, but they differ in aesthetics, comfort, compliance demands, cost and which cases each handles best. This side-by-side comparison helps you choose with confidence.
intro: Choosing between Invisalign and traditional braces is one of the first decisions orthodontic patients face. Both systems can produce beautiful, functional results — but they work very differently and suit different patients. The right answer depends on the complexity of your case, your lifestyle, your compliance habits and your priorities around aesthetics and comfort.

This article breaks down every meaningful comparison point between the two systems so that patients considering orthodontic treatment at [Smile Dental Arts Centre](/appointments) in Markham can arrive at their consultation already oriented to the options. We cover aesthetics, comfort, hygiene, cost, treatment time, suitability and what happens when treatment is complete.

blocks.text: This is the dimension most patients consider first, and Invisalign wins clearly. The aligners are made from a clear, medical-grade thermoplastic that is essentially invisible at normal conversational distances. Most people wearing Invisalign report that friends and colleagues do not notice they are in orthodontic treatment unless told directly. Tooth-coloured attachments bonded to some teeth are slightly visible on close inspection but remain far more discreet than metal brackets.

Traditional metal braces are visible from a distance. Ceramic (tooth-coloured) braces are less noticeable than metal but still more visible than Invisalign aligners, and the ceramic brackets can stain over time if the patient consumes a lot of coffee, tea or curry. For adults in professional environments or teenagers navigating social sensitivity around their appearance, aesthetics is often the deciding factor in favour of Invisalign.

sections.heading: Comfort: Aligners vs. Brackets and Wires

blocks.text: Invisalign aligners are smooth plastic — they do not have sharp edges or protruding wires that can poke and cut the inside of the cheek or lip. The most common discomfort with Invisalign is pressure when a new aligner set is inserted, typically lasting 24–72 hours. Patients consistently rate this as mild to moderate on pain scales, manageable with ibuprofen.

Traditional braces cause more varied discomfort. The wires and brackets rub against the soft tissue of cheeks and lips until calluses form — typically over the first four to six weeks. Wax placed over sharp spots provides relief but is inconvenient. After adjustment appointments, soreness lasting two to four days is common as the wire is tightened. Accidental impacts — a ball to the face, a poorly judged bite of food — can break a bracket or bend a wire, requiring an emergency visit.

items: Invisalign: smooth plastic; main discomfort is pressure when changing aligner sets.
Braces: brackets and wires cause soft tissue irritation; adjustment soreness after each visit.
Braces: loose brackets or broken wires require urgent appointments that Invisalign does not.
Invisalign: no food restrictions because aligners are removed for eating.
Braces: sticky, hard and chewy foods must be avoided for the entire treatment duration.

blocks.text: Oral hygiene with traditional braces is genuinely more difficult than with Invisalign. Brackets and wires create dozens of new nooks where plaque and food debris accumulate. Special interdental brushes, floss threaders and water flossers are recommended but even diligent patients often show increased decalcification (white spots on enamel) around brackets after treatment. The [Canadian Dental Association](https://www.cda-adc.ca/) recommends additional professional cleanings during braces treatment to manage this risk.

With Invisalign, oral hygiene is almost identical to normal — remove the aligners, brush and floss as usual, rinse the aligner, replace it. The caveat is that the aligners themselves must be cleaned regularly to prevent bacterial and odour buildup: rinsing them with cool water every time they are removed, brushing them gently with a soft brush morning and evening, and soaking them in Invisalign cleaning crystals or a diluted retainer cleaner weekly.

sections.heading: Treatment Time: How Each System Compares

blocks.text: For mild to moderate cases, treatment times are broadly similar — 12 to 18 months is typical for both systems. For complex cases involving significant overbite, underbite or significant crowding, braces have historically been faster, though this gap has narrowed substantially as Invisalign technology and clinical protocols have improved. Very complex cases may still be better managed with braces on a pure timeline basis.

The critical variable for Invisalign timeline is compliance. Aligners must be worn 20–22 hours per day — and the patient is in control of this. Braces work around the clock regardless of patient behaviour. Highly motivated, compliant patients often finish Invisalign treatment at or ahead of schedule. Patients who remove aligners too frequently can extend their treatment significantly. See our full [Invisalign Markham guide](/blog/invisalign-markham-cost-timeline) for timeline details.

Traditional braces in Markham typically cost $3,500 to $6,000 for comprehensive treatment. Invisalign ranges from $3,000 to $7,500 for a comparable case. Historically Invisalign was premium-priced; the gap has narrowed considerably. For mild cases treated with Invisalign Lite, Invisalign can actually be less expensive than full braces. Most dental insurance plans treat Invisalign and braces identically under orthodontic benefits, so the same lifetime maximum applies to both.

One cost consideration favoring braces: with braces, the orthodontist controls every movement at adjustment appointments and has more direct influence over the outcome, potentially reducing the need for refinements. With Invisalign, refinements (additional aligner stages when teeth have not fully reached planned positions at the end of the original series) are common in complex cases. Confirm whether refinements are included in your quoted fee.

sections.heading: Which Cases Each System Handles Best

blocks.text: Invisalign is excellent for: mild to moderate crowding and spacing, simple overbite and overjet corrections, tooth rotations in most positions, and patients with high aesthetic priorities. It is highly effective for most adult cases and for teens with strong compliance. Braces have an advantage for: complex bite corrections (significant class III underbites, severe skeletal discrepancies), patients who know they will not comply consistently with removable appliances, and some cases requiring precise control of root position.

The honest answer is that both systems, in the hands of an experienced clinician with a well-developed digital treatment plan, produce excellent outcomes for the vast majority of orthodontic patients. The choice often comes down to lifestyle preference rather than clinical necessity. Dr. Kadivar will advise you clearly if your case has features better suited to one system over the other.

sections.heading: Making the Decision at Your Consultation

blocks.text: The best way to choose between Invisalign and braces is to have a thorough clinical assessment — ideally with digital photos, x-rays and a 3D intraoral scan — so you can see a realistic prediction of your treatment outcome before committing. At Smile Dental Arts Centre, we use the iTero scanner for Invisalign simulations and provide written treatment plans comparing options for every new orthodontic patient.

[Book a consultation](/appointments) with Dr. Neda Kadivar at our Markham clinic. We will evaluate your specific case, show you a ClinCheck simulation of your Invisalign outcome, and give you an honest assessment of whether braces would serve you better in any way. The [Canadian Orthodontic Association](https://www.cao-aco.org/) recommends basing orthodontic decisions on individual clinical factors, not advertising — and so do we.

title: Can Adults Get Invisalign? Age Limits Explained
seoTitle: Can Adults Get Invisalign? Age Limits Explained | Smile Dental Arts Centre Markham
metaDescription: There is no upper age limit for Invisalign. Learn why adult orthodontics is so common, what differences to expect compared to teen treatment, and whether your case qualifies.
excerpt: There is no upper age limit for Invisalign — adults in their 40s, 60s and even 70s successfully complete orthodontic treatment every day. This article explains why adult orthodontics has surged in popularity, what differences adults should expect compared to teens, and the clinical factors that determine candidacy.
intro: One of the most persistent myths about orthodontic treatment is that braces and clear aligners are only for teenagers. The reality is quite different: adults represent a growing share of orthodontic patients in Canada, and the [Canadian Orthodontic Association](https://www.cao-aco.org/) estimates that roughly one in four orthodontic patients today is an adult. Invisalign, which is discrete and removable, has been particularly popular with working professionals and parents who want to improve their smile without the visibility of metal braces.

This article explains why adult orthodontic treatment is not only possible but increasingly common, what clinical differences exist between adult and teenage treatment, the specific conditions that affect candidacy, and what a typical adult Invisalign experience at [Smile Dental Arts Centre](/appointments) looks like.

blocks.text: Adults pursue orthodontic treatment for a wide range of reasons. Many had braces as teenagers but stopped wearing their retainers, allowing their teeth to shift over the years. Others never received orthodontic treatment at all — either because their families could not afford it, because the options available were unappealing, or because their alignment was borderline and not treated in childhood. Life changes also create new demand: many adults find themselves focusing on their smile after a career promotion, a divorce, or simply reaching an age where they have discretionary income to invest in themselves.

The rise of Invisalign has been the single biggest driver of adult orthodontic uptake. Unlike metal braces — which many adults find unacceptable in professional and social settings — Invisalign's clear aligners are virtually invisible. This aesthetics difference removes the primary barrier that kept many adults from pursuing treatment for decades. The removability for eating and social occasions also fits adult lifestyles in ways that fixed braces do not.

sections.heading: Is There an Upper Age Limit for Invisalign?

blocks.text: No — there is no maximum age for Invisalign treatment. Teeth can be moved at any age, because the biological process of bone remodelling that allows orthodontic movement does not stop when we reach adulthood. A 65-year-old with healthy teeth and gums can undergo Invisalign treatment just as effectively as a 25-year-old. Age itself is not a clinical contraindication.

The minimum age for Invisalign is more clinically meaningful: Invisalign should not begin until all adult teeth have erupted, which typically occurs around age 12–14. Invisalign Teen is designed for younger adolescents with most adult teeth present but potentially still erupting. Adult Invisalign — the standard comprehensive product — is appropriate for anyone whose adult teeth are fully present, regardless of whether that person is 18 or 80.

Key fact: The oldest Invisalign patient at our Markham clinic was in their early 70s. Provided the teeth and supporting structures are healthy, age is never the deciding factor in Invisalign candidacy.

sections.heading: Differences Between Adult and Teen Treatment

blocks.text: Biological differences between adult and adolescent bone do affect treatment in subtle ways. Adult bone is denser and less plastic than adolescent bone — teeth move slightly more slowly, and some movements require more time or force to accomplish. This means adult Invisalign cases can sometimes take a few months longer than a comparable teen case. However, adult compliance is typically superior: adults are generally more motivated and consistent about wearing their aligners than teenagers, which often compensates for any biological slowdown.

Adults are also more likely to present with pre-existing dental work — crowns, bridges, veneers, implants and large fillings — that must be factored into the treatment plan. Invisalign aligners cannot move dental implants (the titanium post is permanently fused to the bone), so cases where an implant is adjacent to the area being treated require careful planning. Dr. Kadivar reviews all existing restorations during your records appointment before beginning any treatment plan.

sections.heading: Gum Health: The Most Important Prerequisite

blocks.text: The most critical prerequisite for adult Invisalign — even more important than the alignment issues being treated — is healthy gums. Adults are more likely than teenagers to have had some degree of gum disease (periodontitis), which causes bone loss around the teeth. Attempting orthodontic tooth movement in a mouth with uncontrolled active gum disease can accelerate that bone loss and cause tooth mobility or loss. For this reason, any active periodontal disease must be treated and stabilised before Invisalign begins.

This is not a barrier that rules most adults out — it simply requires that gum disease be identified and treated first, which is straightforward and usually involves a deep cleaning (scaling and root planing) and a course of improved home care. Once the gum health is stable, confirmed by a professional assessment, Invisalign can proceed safely. Our clinic performs a thorough gum health assessment at the Invisalign records appointment.

sections.heading: What Types of Problems Can Adult Invisalign Fix?

blocks.text: The range of problems Invisalign can address for adults spans from simple cosmetic corrections — mild crowding of the front teeth, small gaps — to more significant functional corrections including overbite, underbite, crossbite and significant crowding across multiple teeth. Invisalign technology has improved dramatically since the system launched in 1999, and cases that previously required braces can now be handled with aligners in experienced hands.

items: Crowded teeth — the most common reason adults seek Invisalign; mild to moderate crowding is highly predictable.
Spacing and gaps — including gap-closure cases after orthodontic relapse from stopped retainer use.
Overbite — excess vertical overlap of front teeth; correctable with bite ramps built into aligners.
Open bite — where upper and lower front teeth do not meet; Invisalign has made significant inroads here.
Crossbite — upper and lower teeth meeting in the wrong lateral relationship; very correctable with aligners.

sections.heading: Can Invisalign Work with Existing Dental Work?

blocks.text: Invisalign can be used in mouths with crowns, veneers, bonding and large composite fillings with careful planning. Attachments placed on existing restorations may not bond as reliably as on natural enamel, which is factored into the treatment design. Teeth with veneers are moved with particular care because excess tipping forces can stress the veneer margin. In some cases, Dr. Kadivar will recommend replacing an old veneer before beginning Invisalign to ensure better predictability.

Bridges cannot be separated by aligners — the three teeth in a three-unit bridge move as a single unit. If you have a bridge adjacent to the teeth being moved, the treatment plan is designed around that constraint. Implants, as noted, cannot be moved themselves but the teeth around them can be repositioned to improve the overall bite. A detailed records review will identify all such considerations before your first aligner is fabricated.

sections.heading: Taking the First Step in Markham

blocks.text: If you have been waiting until you are old enough, rich enough, or no longer worried about what colleagues will think of braces — the answer is: Invisalign was made for you. Adults make excellent Invisalign patients precisely because they are motivated, compliant and clear about their goals. The investment pays off for decades, every time you smile in a photograph, a meeting or a mirror.

Dr. Neda Kadivar at Smile Dental Arts Centre in Markham offers complimentary Invisalign consultations that include a digital scan, a ClinCheck smile simulation and a written cost estimate. There is no pressure and no obligation. [Book your consultation](/appointments) and see what your smile could look like in 12–18 months.

title: How to Care for Your Invisalign Trays
seoTitle: How to Care for Invisalign Trays | Markham | Smile Dental Arts Centre
metaDescription: Keep your Invisalign trays clean, clear and odour-free with these care tips from Dr. Neda Kadivar. Learn what to clean them with, what to avoid, and common mistakes to skip.
primaryKeyword: how to care for invisalign trays
excerpt: Invisalign trays that are not cleaned properly turn cloudy, develop odour and harbour bacteria. This guide covers the daily cleaning routine, what products to avoid, how to handle trays safely and what to do if a tray is lost or damaged.
intro: Invisalign aligners do their job invisibly — but only if they stay clear. Cloudy, stained or odorous trays undermine both the aesthetics and hygiene of your treatment. Fortunately, keeping them in perfect condition requires only a few minutes of simple maintenance per day, and the habits are easy to build once you understand why each step matters.

This guide from Dr. Neda Kadivar at [Smile Dental Arts Centre](/appointments) covers the complete daily care routine for Invisalign trays, the products to avoid, common mistakes that damage or discolour aligners, and what to do in less-common situations like a broken or lost tray.

blocks.text: Every time you remove your aligners — for meals, for brushing, or for a planned removal during an event — rinse them immediately under cool running water. Saliva dries on the aligner surface and begins to develop odour and cloudiness within hours if the tray is not rinsed. This single habit, done consistently, prevents the majority of maintenance problems patients experience with their aligners.

Morning and evening, give each aligner a more thorough cleaning: add a small amount of clear, unscented soap (plain dish soap or hand soap works well) and gently scrub all surfaces — inside, outside, and the attachment pockets — with a dedicated soft toothbrush. Rinse thoroughly to remove all soap. This twice-daily scrub removes the biofilm that builds up on aligner surfaces and keeps the plastic clear and odour-free.

items: Rinse immediately in cool water every time you remove your aligners.
Brush with clear unscented soap morning and evening — never toothpaste.
Store in the case provided when not in your mouth — never wrap in a napkin.
Brush your teeth before reinserting aligners so you are not trapping food underneath.
Soak weekly in Invisalign cleaning crystals or a diluted retainer cleaning solution.

blocks.text: **Toothpaste is the most common mistake.** Most toothpastes contain mild abrasives that scratch the aligner surface microscopically — these scratches harbour bacteria and make the aligner appear cloudy. Use only clear, unscented soap for brushing aligners. Whitening toothpastes are particularly abrasive and cause visible cloudiness within days.

**Hot water** is equally damaging — it warps the thermoplastic material, distorting the aligner so it no longer fits accurately. Always rinse and clean with cool or lukewarm water. Similarly, leaving aligners in a hot car or direct sunlight will warp them permanently. **Mouthwash** containing alcohol can discolour or weaken the plastic; if you use mouthwash, remove your aligners first and reinsert after rinsing.
Never eat or drink coloured beverages with aligners in. Coffee, tea, red wine and juices stain the plastic permanently within days. Water only — always — while wearing your trays.

Once a week, soak your aligners for the time specified on the packaging of Invisalign cleaning crystals (available from our clinic) or a compatible retainer cleaning tablet. The soak dissolves mineral buildup and kills bacteria that daily brushing leaves behind. Remove the aligners from the solution, give them a final brush under cool water, and they should look essentially new — clear, odourless and fitting snugly.

Some patients prefer to use a 50/50 dilution of white vinegar and water as a weekly soak. This is effective and economical but the aligners must be rinsed extremely thoroughly afterward — any residual vinegar taste will make the aligners unpleasant to wear. The commercial cleaning crystals are more convenient and specifically formulated for the plastic Invisalign uses.

Always store aligners in their case when they are not in your mouth. The case protects them from contamination, accidental damage and — most importantly — loss. Restaurant tables, bathroom counters and jacket pockets are all places where aligners disappear. A napkin-wrapped aligner is nearly indistinguishable from a used tissue and is discarded by cleaning staff with alarming frequency. Your case prevents all of this.

Keep your previous set of aligners as a backup. When you move to a new set, do not discard the previous week's set immediately. If your new aligners are lost or damaged early in their two-week wear cycle, you can revert to the previous set while a replacement is fabricated — this is much better than having no aligner in place for two to three weeks, which can allow minor tooth relapse.

sections.heading: What to Do If a Tray Is Lost or Broken

blocks.text: Contact our clinic immediately if an aligner is lost or breaks. Do not panic — replacements can be ordered, though fabrication takes one to two weeks. In the interim, if you are early in your wear cycle (first few days of a new set), revert to the previous set. If you are near the end of your wear cycle (day 10 or later of a 14-day set), Dr. Kadivar may advise moving directly to the next set in the series — the progression is usually small enough that the next aligner will fit.

Avoid attempting to repair a cracked or broken aligner with household adhesives. These products are not biocompatible for oral use and can contaminate the aligner surface with harmful chemicals. A broken aligner that still fits without sharp edges may be safe to continue wearing temporarily; one with sharp edges that could cut soft tissue should not be worn until replaced.

One of Invisalign's major advantages over braces is simplified oral hygiene. But this advantage only materialises if you actually remove the aligners before eating and brush before reinserting them. Placing aligners over unclean teeth traps food and bacteria in close contact with the enamel surface for hours — which can accelerate decay. The small inconvenience of carrying a travel toothbrush is worth the peace of mind that your teeth are protected.

Flossing is unrestricted with Invisalign — no floss threaders or special tools needed. Brush and floss normally every morning and evening with the aligners removed. If you cannot brush after a meal before reinserting, at minimum rinse your mouth vigorously with water to dislodge food debris before putting the aligner back in. Never go to sleep with dirty teeth inside your aligners.

sections.heading: Care at the End of Each Aligner Set

blocks.text: At the end of each two-week (or one-week, if Dr. Kadivar has specified a faster schedule) wear cycle, give the retiring aligner a final thorough clean and store it in its numbered bag. Do not discard it — keep the retired sets in order as a record of your progress and as a backup supply. Moving to your next aligner is an exciting moment — each set represents meaningful tooth movement toward your final smile.

If your new aligner feels tight — which it should — that is entirely normal. The tightness means it is actively moving your teeth. Insert it gently using equal fingertip pressure across the aligner surface, not just biting it in (biting in stresses the attachment pockets and can crack the plastic). Use an Aligner Seater (Chewies) — a small silicone roll you bite down on — to fully seat the aligner over your teeth and attachment bumps.

title: Invisalign for Teens: A Parent's Guide
seoTitle: Invisalign for Teens: A Parent's Guide | Markham | Smile Dental Arts Centre
metaDescription: Is Invisalign right for your teen? Learn about Invisalign Teen features, compliance indicators, cost, how it compares to braces and what to expect from treatment in Markham.
excerpt: Invisalign Teen is designed specifically for adolescent patients, with compliance indicators, replacement aligners for lost trays and compensation for still-erupting teeth. This parent's guide covers everything you need to know before deciding.
intro: Teenagers are often resistant to the idea of traditional metal braces — the visibility, the dietary restrictions and the mouth soreness can feel socially and physically burdensome at an already self-conscious age. Invisalign Teen offers an alternative that many adolescents find far more acceptable: clear, removable aligners that most classmates will never notice. But is it the right choice for your child's specific orthodontic needs?

This guide for parents covers the features that make Invisalign Teen different from the adult version, how to assess whether your teenager has the discipline the system requires, what the treatment involves from a clinical standpoint, and how to manage cost and insurance in Ontario. For a broader comparison of aligners versus braces, see our [Invisalign vs. braces article](/blog/invisalign-vs-braces).

blocks.text: Invisalign Teen is a version of the Invisalign system designed specifically for adolescent patients, with several features added to address the realities of teenage life. The most important difference is the inclusion of compliance indicators — small dots on the aligners that fade from blue to clear with wear. These indicators provide an objective measure of how many hours per day the aligner is being worn, which is helpful for both parents checking in and Dr. Kadivar monitoring treatment progress at check-up appointments.

Invisalign Teen also includes up to six replacement aligners as part of the standard fee — because teenagers lose things. Each replacement set is identical to the original lost tray, fabricated and shipped at no additional cost within the included replacement allowance. The system also accommodates still-erupting teeth: aligner shapes can include eruption tabs — raised areas in the plastic — that hold space for incoming adult teeth while the patient is in active treatment.

sections.heading: Is Your Teen a Good Candidate?

blocks.text: The first clinical criterion is that most adult teeth must be present. Invisalign Teen is typically appropriate from around age 12 or 13 for most patients, though this varies. A consultation with Dr. Kadivar, including an x-ray to assess root development, will confirm readiness. Teens with significant skeletal discrepancies — a pronounced underbite or overbite with a jaw component, for example — may be better served by braces with auxiliary appliances, or may need to wait for jaw growth to complete before definitive treatment.

The more important assessment for teens is compliance personality. Invisalign Teen requires the aligner to be in the mouth for 20–22 hours every day. A teenager who will reliably wear the aligners, keep them clean, and remember them after removing them for lunch is an excellent candidate. A teenager who already struggles with consistent habits around homework, medication or daily routines may have a better outcome with fixed braces that do not require self-discipline. This is an honest conversation to have with your child before choosing.

Parent tip: Ask Dr. Kadivar to show you the compliance indicator dots at your teen's check-up appointments. If the dots are still intensely blue at an appointment where they should be fading, it is a clear, objective signal that wearing time needs to improve — without the need for a confrontational conversation at home.

sections.heading: What the Treatment Process Looks Like

blocks.text: Treatment begins with a records appointment: digital photos, panoramic and periapical x-rays, and an intraoral scan with the iTero element scanner (no putty impressions). These records are sent to Invisalign's technicians who create a ClinCheck digital treatment simulation — a visual before-and-after that your teen can see before any treatment starts. Once the treatment plan is approved, the aligners are fabricated and typically arrive within two to three weeks.

At the delivery appointment, small tooth-coloured attachments are bonded to specific teeth to help the aligners apply more precise forces. Your teen goes home with the first three to four sets of aligners and instructions for changing them every one to two weeks. Check-up appointments every six to ten weeks monitor progress. Treatment runs six to 24 months depending on case complexity.

sections.heading: Comparing Invisalign Teen to Traditional Braces for Teenagers

blocks.text: Beyond aesthetics, Invisalign Teen has several practical advantages for teenagers. Dietary freedom — no prohibition on popcorn, gum, apples or hard candies — means less social friction at parties, school events and restaurants. Oral hygiene is normal, reducing the risk of decalcification marks around brackets. Contact sports and band/choir participation are all simpler without fixed metal hardware in the mouth.

Traditional braces remain preferable for some teenage cases: those involving significant bite correction that Invisalign handles less predictably, those where compliance is expected to be inconsistent, and cases where the orthodontic treatment needs to work continuously without any reliance on patient cooperation. The choice is best made after a clinical examination, not based on advertising.

sections.heading: Cost and Insurance for Teen Invisalign in Ontario

blocks.text: Invisalign Teen in Markham typically costs $4,500 to $7,000 for comprehensive treatment. Most Ontario family dental plans include an orthodontic benefit of $1,500 to $3,500 lifetime per dependent child, which applies equally to Invisalign Teen and traditional braces. There is generally no premium for choosing Invisalign over braces from an insurance standpoint, as long as the plan covers orthodontics for dependents.

At Smile Dental Arts Centre we submit orthodontic pre-determinations before beginning treatment, so you know exactly what your plan will contribute before your teen wears their first aligner. Monthly payment plans are available for the remaining balance. Many families find that spreading the out-of-pocket portion over 18–24 months makes the investment very manageable alongside other household expenses.

sections.heading: Helping Your Teen Succeed with Invisalign

blocks.text: Parental involvement makes a meaningful difference in teen Invisalign outcomes. Establishing a daily routine where aligner wear, cleaning and storage are habitual — attached to existing routines like morning and evening toothbrushing — helps compliance become automatic rather than a daily decision. Some parents set a phone alarm reminder at mealtimes as a signal to reinsert aligners after eating.

Helping your teen understand that the compliance indicators are not a surveillance tool but a useful self-monitoring aid reframes them positively. Teens who understand that skipping aligner wear extends their treatment time — meaning more months of wearing aligners — are often more motivated than those who see it as a parental requirement. The treatment goal belongs to the patient, not the parent, and framing it that way consistently produces better outcomes.

sections.heading: Next Steps: Booking a Teen Invisalign Consultation in Markham

blocks.text: A complimentary Invisalign Teen consultation at Smile Dental Arts Centre includes an iTero intraoral scan, a review of your teen's orthodontic needs and timeline, a ClinCheck smile simulation and a written cost and insurance estimate. The consultation is a no-pressure appointment — we want you and your teen to have all the information needed to make the right decision together.

Dr. Neda Kadivar is a certified Invisalign provider serving Markham, Unionville and the surrounding communities. Our clinic is open Monday through Friday and every other Saturday for your convenience. [Book a consultation](/appointments) for your teen today.

title: Signs You Might Need Orthodontic Treatment
seoTitle: Signs You Need Orthodontic Treatment | Markham | Smile Dental Arts Centre
metaDescription: Crowded teeth, jaw pain, difficulty chewing — these are signs orthodontic treatment may help. Learn which symptoms indicate a need for evaluation by a Markham dentist.
excerpt: Orthodontic problems are not always obvious. Some — like crowded teeth or a gap — are visible in the mirror. Others, like a misaligned bite or jaw joint strain, present as symptoms you might not connect to your teeth at all. This guide identifies the signs that warrant an orthodontic evaluation.
intro: Most people know orthodontic treatment is about straightening teeth — but the reasons to pursue it extend well beyond aesthetics. Bite alignment affects how efficiently you chew, how evenly your teeth wear, whether your jaw joints are under strain, and how successfully you can clean your teeth at home. Recognising the signs that something is off is the first step toward getting a proper evaluation.

This article outlines the most common visible and non-visible signals that orthodontic assessment is warranted, explains what each symptom might indicate clinically, and describes what an evaluation at [Smile Dental Arts Centre](/appointments) in Markham involves.

blocks.text: The most immediately obvious orthodontic issues are those you can see directly: teeth that overlap each other, teeth that are rotated out of alignment with their neighbours, a noticeable gap between the front teeth (diastema), or upper front teeth that dramatically protrude or sit far behind the lower teeth. These visible misalignments are the scenarios most people associate with needing braces or Invisalign.

items: **Crowding** — teeth overlapping, stacked or rotated due to insufficient arch space.
**Spacing** — gaps between teeth, most commonly between the upper front teeth.
**Overjet** — upper front teeth protrude significantly forward beyond the lower teeth.
**Open bite** — upper and lower front teeth do not touch when biting; a gap exists between them.
**Crossbite** — upper teeth sit inside (rather than outside) lower teeth in any part of the arch.

blocks.text: Bite misalignment — called malocclusion — is not always obvious visually. Some patients have teeth that look reasonably straight but whose bite does not function correctly. Signs of bite problems include biting the inside of your cheeks or tongue repeatedly, food that consistently catches or packs between certain teeth, difficulty biting into certain foods, and uneven wear on specific teeth that your dentist points out on x-rays.

An overbite — where the upper front teeth cover too much of the lower front teeth when biting — can cause the lower teeth to bite into the palate (roof of the mouth), causing tissue irritation and wear. An underbite — where the lower jaw extends beyond the upper — affects chewing efficiency and can cause accelerated wear on the lower front teeth. Both are very correctable with orthodontic treatment, often with Invisalign for mild to moderate cases.

Jaw joint discomfort — clicking, popping, locking or pain in the TMJ (temporomandibular joint) — can be caused or worsened by bite misalignment. When the upper and lower teeth do not come together evenly, the jaw muscles and joints must compensate with every bite and swallow, creating chronic strain. Not all TMJ problems are orthodontic in origin, but a significant proportion improve when the bite is corrected. Our [TMJ and your bite article](/blog/tmj-pain-and-your-bite) covers this connection in detail.

Headaches, particularly those felt at the temples or behind the eyes and worse in the morning, can also be a sign of bite-related muscle clenching. Patients who grind or clench at night — which is often driven or worsened by an uneven bite — may find that orthodontic correction reduces the grinding habit and the headaches associated with it. This is worth discussing at your consultation if you experience morning headaches or jaw stiffness.

Crowded teeth are more than an aesthetic issue — they are a hygiene issue. When teeth overlap, toothbrush bristles cannot reach every surface and floss cannot pass cleanly through the contact points. These uncleaned areas accumulate plaque that causes decay and gum disease over time. Patients with crowded teeth often have more cavities between teeth and more gum inflammation than patients with well-aligned dentition, even when their brushing habits are identical.

If your dentist or hygienist consistently points out areas of plaque accumulation that are difficult to clean because of tooth overlap or crowding, that is a sign that orthodontic correction would improve not just your smile but your long-term periodontal health. Straighter teeth are genuinely healthier teeth, all other factors being equal.

sections.heading: Early Signs in Children to Watch For

blocks.text: The [Canadian Dental Association](https://www.cda-adc.ca/) recommends that children have their first orthodontic assessment by age seven, even if treatment is not needed yet. At this age, the dentist can identify developing problems — narrow arches, crowding that will worsen as permanent teeth erupt, early crossbites — and advise on whether early intervention (phase one treatment) would simplify later comprehensive treatment or whether watchful waiting is appropriate.

Early signs in children that warrant evaluation: persistent thumb or finger sucking beyond age five or six (which can push the front teeth forward), mouth breathing (which affects jaw development), speech difficulties, asymmetrical jaw growth, difficulty chewing, and baby teeth that are slow to fall out or adult teeth that are slow to erupt. None of these guarantee orthodontic treatment is needed, but all are reasons to have an assessment.

sections.heading: When Orthodontic Problems Are Not Obvious

blocks.text: Some bite problems are subtle enough that patients do not notice them until a dentist identifies them on x-rays or during a clinical examination. A posterior crossbite, for example, may cause no noticeable symptoms but results in the jaw shifting to one side during biting, creating asymmetric muscle and joint loading over time. A deep bite — significant overbite — may feel normal to the patient while slowly grinding down the lower front teeth.

This is one reason regular dental check-ups are important even for patients who feel fine. Dr. Kadivar checks bite alignment and tooth wear as part of every comprehensive examination. If she identifies a developing orthodontic issue, she will explain what she has found, what the implications are if left unaddressed, and what the treatment options are — without any pressure to proceed immediately.

An orthodontic evaluation at Smile Dental Arts Centre includes a clinical examination of your bite, tooth alignment, jaw joints and gum health, panoramic and periapical x-rays to assess roots and bone, and — for Invisalign candidates — a digital intraoral scan. If orthodontic treatment is recommended, Dr. Kadivar will explain the options (Invisalign, braces or specialist referral for complex cases), expected treatment time and cost.

The evaluation is thorough and unhurried — we do not rush orthodontic assessments because the decision involves a meaningful time and financial commitment. [Book an orthodontic evaluation](/appointments) at our Markham clinic to get a clear picture of your current bite health and what — if anything — would benefit from treatment.

title: Night Guards vs. Invisalign: Not the Same Thing
seoTitle: Night Guards vs. Invisalign: What's the Difference? | Smile Dental Arts Centre
metaDescription: Night guards and Invisalign aligners look similar but serve completely different purposes. Learn what each does, why you cannot use one as a substitute for the other, and when you need both.
excerpt: Night guards and Invisalign aligners look nearly identical to the untrained eye, which leads many patients to wonder if one can substitute for the other. They cannot — they are designed for fundamentally different purposes and using one as the other causes damage.
intro: Patients regularly ask whether they can use their Invisalign aligners as night guards, or vice versa. The two appliances look remarkably similar — both are clear, removable, custom-fitted plastic trays — and the confusion is understandable. But they are built for completely different purposes from different materials, and substituting one for the other can damage your teeth, your aligners or both.

This article explains what each appliance does, why the materials and designs differ, what happens when patients use one in place of the other, and when some patients legitimately need both — wearing a night guard over or instead of their retainer to protect their orthodontic results from nocturnal grinding.

blocks.text: A night guard (also called an occlusal splint or bruxism guard) is designed to protect teeth from the forces of bruxism — grinding and clenching during sleep. The guard absorbs the energy of grinding on its surface rather than allowing it to transfer into the tooth enamel, which is far less resilient. Over time, unchecked bruxism can fracture cusps, wear enamel flat, cause temperature sensitivity, crack fillings and crowns, and damage the temporomandibular joint.

Night guards are made from acrylic, ethylene-vinyl acetate (EVA), or a hard-soft laminate, depending on the clinical design preferred. Custom-fitted guards from a dental lab provide far better protection and comfort than over-the-counter boil-and-bite versions, which are bulky, imprecise and easily deformed under clenching forces. The guard should be thick enough to provide a meaningful cushioning layer — typically 2–4 mm — which Invisalign aligners are not.

Invisalign aligners are made from a thin, precisely engineered thermoplastic called SmartTrack. The material is chosen for its specific elastic memory — it applies controlled, gentle forces to teeth to move them incrementally toward their planned positions. The thinness and material formulation are what makes Invisalign comfortable and effective as an orthodontic appliance.

The very properties that make Invisalign work well for orthodontics make it terrible as a bruxism guard. SmartTrack is thin and relatively soft compared to occlusal splint acrylic — it is not designed to absorb the repeated, forceful impact of grinding. Patients who grind in their Invisalign aligners chew through the aligner plastic within days, warping the aligner and potentially cracking it. This compromises fit, tooth movement and the hygiene of the aligner simultaneously.

sections.heading: Why You Cannot Use Invisalign as a Night Guard

blocks.text: Wearing Invisalign during sleep if you have a grinding habit is one of the most common ways patients damage their aligners. The grinding forces distort the aligner shape — changing the pressures applied to teeth and potentially moving teeth in unintended directions. The plastic surface becomes pitted and rough, harbouring bacteria. In severe grinding cases the aligner cracks or fractures within a week, requiring replacement before the normal two-week wear cycle has completed.

More importantly, an Invisalign aligner does not protect your teeth from grinding forces — it simply moves those forces from enamel-on-enamel contact to enamel-on-plastic-on-enamel contact, which provides minimal protective value. The aligner is not thick or rigid enough to distribute grinding forces the way a proper occlusal splint does. If you have bruxism, you need a night guard regardless of whether you are in Invisalign treatment.

If you are in Invisalign treatment and know you grind at night, tell Dr. Kadivar before treatment begins. A thin hard acrylic night guard can be fabricated to wear over your Invisalign aligners at night, protecting both the aligner and your teeth simultaneously.

Night guards are not designed to move teeth — but some designs can apply inadvertent forces that cause minor shifting if worn incorrectly or worn over a very long period with significant changes in the underlying bite. Soft EVA guards that adapt to the teeth snugly can, in theory, maintain teeth in positions that would otherwise shift — which is why some dentists recommend wearing a night guard after orthodontic treatment as a combined bruxism guard and retainer.

Hard occlusal splints — the most clinically effective type of night guard for significant bruxism — should be made with enough space in the design that they do not apply orthodontic-level forces. These are fitted and checked by the dentist at follow-up appointments to ensure they are not inadvertently affecting the bite over time.

sections.heading: When You Need Both: Invisalign and a Night Guard

blocks.text: Patients who grind at night and also want orthodontic treatment with Invisalign genuinely need both appliances — but using them together is manageable. The most common approach is to wear the Invisalign aligner during the day (the required 20–22 hours includes waking hours), and to wear either a thin night guard over the aligner at night or to switch to wearing the night guard at night and the aligner during all waking hours. The plan is customised based on the severity of grinding.

After Invisalign treatment is complete, the retainer phase also requires thought for bruxers. A standard clear retainer is just as vulnerable to grinding damage as an Invisalign aligner. A hard acrylic night guard that also functions as a retainer — called a Hawley retainer with an occlusal component, or a specifically fabricated bruxism retainer — may be the most practical long-term solution for patients who grind.

sections.heading: Recognising Bruxism: Do You Need a Night Guard?

blocks.text: Many patients who grind their teeth do not know they do it — grinding during sleep is largely unconscious, and sleeping partners sometimes notice it before the grinder does. Signs that you may be grinding include waking with a sore or tight jaw, morning headaches at the temples, excessive wear on your back teeth (visible on x-rays as flattened cusps), chipped teeth at the gum line, and sensitivity to temperature that comes and goes. See our [TMJ pain article](/blog/tmj-pain-and-your-bite) for more on recognising these symptoms.

At your comprehensive examination at Smile Dental Arts Centre, Dr. Kadivar checks for signs of bruxism as part of every routine assessment. If wear patterns suggest grinding is occurring, she will discuss night guard options and, if you are a current or prospective Invisalign patient, how to integrate night guard use with your aligner treatment safely.

sections.heading: Getting the Right Appliance at Our Markham Clinic

blocks.text: Whether you need a night guard, Invisalign, or both, the first step is a clinical evaluation to understand what is happening with your bite, your teeth and your jaw joints. At Smile Dental Arts Centre we do not sell appliances patients do not need — if your wear patterns are mild and your bite is well-aligned, a night guard may be optional rather than urgent. If significant wear is present, we will explain the consequences of delaying and the options available.

[Book an appointment](/appointments) at our Markham clinic to discuss night guards, Invisalign or any other appliance you have questions about. Dr. Neda Kadivar and her team are here Monday through Friday with extended hours and every other Saturday.

title: TMJ Pain and Your Bite: When to See a Dentist
seoTitle: TMJ Pain and Your Bite: When to See a Dentist | Smile Dental Arts Centre Markham
metaDescription: Clicking jaw, morning headaches, difficulty chewing — these are signs of TMJ disorder. Learn how bite alignment contributes to TMJ pain and when to seek dental care in Markham.
excerpt: The temporomandibular joint is one of the most complex joints in the body, and when it is under chronic strain — often from a misaligned bite or bruxism — the symptoms can include jaw pain, clicking, headaches and neck tension. This article explains the connection and what treatment can help.
intro: The temporomandibular joint (TMJ) connects your lower jaw to your skull on each side of your face. It is active in virtually every function of the oral cavity: chewing, speaking, yawning, swallowing. When this joint is under chronic strain — whether from a bite that is not well-aligned, from grinding and clenching, or from injury — the resulting symptoms can range from mild jaw discomfort to debilitating pain that extends into the face, head and neck.

This article explains what causes TMJ disorder, how bite alignment relates to joint health, what symptoms warrant a dental evaluation, and what treatment options are available at [Smile Dental Arts Centre](/appointments) in Markham.

blocks.text: The TMJ is a hinge-and-sliding joint — it both rotates (when you open slightly) and translates forward (when you open wide). A small cartilage disc sits between the ball of the lower jaw and the socket in the skull, cushioning the joint during all these movements. Ligaments stabilise the joint; a group of muscles — the masseter, temporalis, pterygoids and others — control its movement and bear the forces of chewing, which can reach over 100 pounds per square inch on the back teeth.

Because the TMJ operates continuously throughout every waking hour, and often throughout the night for patients who clench or grind, it is susceptible to cumulative strain. Small imbalances — a bite that causes the jaw to deviate slightly to one side to close, for example — translate into thousands of slightly asymmetric joint movements per day, gradually irritating the joint, the disc and the surrounding soft tissue.

sections.heading: How Bite Misalignment Contributes to TMJ Problems

blocks.text: When the upper and lower teeth do not occlude (meet) evenly, the jaw must shift into an unnatural position to achieve maximum tooth contact for chewing. This shift is unconscious — the neuromuscular system adapts automatically to bring as many teeth into contact as possible. The problem is that achieving maximum tooth contact by shifting the jaw also means the TMJ is not in its most anatomically ideal position, creating chronic strain on the joint and the muscles that hold the jaw in that adapted position.

Common bite problems that stress the TMJ include: significant overbite (deep bite), underbite, crossbite, and missing teeth that have allowed adjacent teeth to drift and change the bite. Orthodontic correction — through [Invisalign](/blog/invisalign-markham-cost-timeline) or traditional braces — addresses the root cause in these cases and often produces meaningful improvement in TMJ symptoms once the bite is corrected.

TMJ disorder (also called temporomandibular disorder or TMD) produces a range of symptoms that patients do not always associate with their jaw. The classic presentation includes jaw pain or tenderness, especially on waking, and clicking or popping sounds when opening or closing the mouth. The sounds alone, without pain, are common and not always clinically significant — it is the combination of sound with pain, locking, or limited opening that warrants evaluation.

items: Jaw pain or tenderness on one or both sides, especially on waking.
Clicking, popping or grating sounds in the jaw joint when opening or closing.
Limited jaw opening — inability to open as wide as normal without pain.
Jaw locking — momentary inability to fully open or close the jaw.
Headaches at the temples, behind the eyes or at the base of the skull.
Ear pain, fullness or ringing (tinnitus) without a clear ear cause.
Neck and shoulder tension that worsens with jaw clenching.

sections.heading: The Role of Bruxism in TMJ Strain

blocks.text: Bruxism — the habitual grinding and clenching of teeth — is one of the most significant drivers of TMJ disorder. During sleep, clenching forces can reach two to three times those of normal chewing, applied continuously for hours. The muscles involved become chronically overworked, developing the same kind of tension and soreness that skeletal muscles develop after prolonged exercise. Morning jaw soreness and temporal headaches are classic signatures of nocturnal bruxism.

A custom night guard is the most effective way to protect the joint and teeth from bruxism forces during sleep. It reduces the muscle activity of clenching and prevents the enamel-on-enamel contact that damages teeth over time. If bruxism is also driven by a bite misalignment, addressing the bite issue with orthodontics — including [Invisalign](/dental-services) — may reduce the grinding trigger itself. For more on the night guard side of this discussion, see our [night guards vs. Invisalign article](/blog/night-guards-vs-invisalign).

sections.heading: When to See a Dentist for Jaw Pain

blocks.text: Not every jaw click requires treatment — isolated, painless clicking is common and often benign. However, you should seek a dental evaluation when: jaw pain persists beyond a few days, clicking is accompanied by pain or limited opening, you wake regularly with jaw or temple soreness, or your jaw locks or catches during normal function. Early evaluation allows for conservative treatment before the condition progresses.

If your dentist suspects TMJ disorder they will examine the joint directly — palpating the muscles and joint for tenderness, measuring jaw opening, listening for joint sounds and assessing your bite. X-rays show the bony structures; occasionally an MRI is needed to visualise the cartilage disc. Most TMJ cases are managed by dentists without specialist referral, though complex cases involving significant disc displacement may benefit from evaluation by an oral and maxillofacial specialist.

The great majority of TMJ disorder cases resolve or improve significantly with conservative treatment. **Night guards** reduce clenching forces and allow the muscles and joint to rest during sleep. **Physiotherapy** targeting the jaw muscles — including stretching exercises, heat therapy and manual release techniques — is highly effective for muscle-dominant TMD. **Anti-inflammatory medication** (ibuprofen) during acute flares reduces pain and inflammation. **Stress management** matters enormously: anxiety and stress are major drivers of clenching, and addressing the psychological component produces meaningful clinical improvement.

When bite misalignment is a clear contributing factor, orthodontic treatment is appropriate. When missing teeth have caused bite collapse, dental restoration (including implants, crowns or dentures) addresses the underlying structural problem. Surgical intervention is rarely necessary and is reserved for disc displacement that does not respond to conservative treatment.

Dr. Neda Kadivar has significant experience in diagnosing and managing TMJ disorder in the context of overall bite health. At Smile Dental Arts Centre, a TMJ evaluation includes a comprehensive bite analysis, muscle palpation, a review of your symptom history and — where orthodontic issues are suspected — a ClinCheck simulation showing what bite correction would involve. Treatment plans are conservative and sequenced: the simplest effective intervention first, with escalation only if needed.

[Book an appointment](/appointments) in Markham if you are experiencing any of the symptoms described above. TMJ problems that are addressed early respond much better to conservative treatment than those that have been present for years. We are available Monday through Friday with extended evening hours and every other Saturday.

title: How Much Does Invisalign Really Cost After Insurance?
seoTitle: Invisalign Cost After Insurance in Ontario | Smile Dental Arts Centre Markham
metaDescription: Wondering what Invisalign costs out-of-pocket after insurance in Ontario? Learn what plans typically cover, how to maximise your benefit and what financing options are available.
excerpt: Most Ontario dental plans include an orthodontic benefit that significantly reduces Invisalign costs — but understanding what you will actually pay out-of-pocket requires knowing exactly how your plan works. This guide breaks it down clearly.
intro: The headline price for Invisalign in Markham is typically $3,000 to $7,500 — but for most patients with employer-sponsored dental benefits, the actual out-of-pocket cost is considerably lower. Ontario group dental plans almost universally include an orthodontic benefit, and that benefit applies to Invisalign just as it applies to traditional braces, making the choice between the two a matter of clinical fit rather than insurance penalty.

This guide explains exactly how orthodontic insurance benefits work in Ontario, what a typical benefit covers and what it leaves uncovered, how to read your benefit booklet, and what financing options are available at [Smile Dental Arts Centre](/appointments) for the remaining balance after insurance.

blocks.text: Orthodontic benefits in Ontario group plans typically operate differently from regular dental benefits. Rather than covering a percentage of each appointment, orthodontic benefits are usually paid as a percentage of the total treatment fee — commonly 50 percent — up to a lifetime maximum per covered person. The lifetime maximum is the most important number to know: it applies once per covered person for their lifetime under the plan, not per year.

For example, a plan with 50 percent coverage and a $2,500 lifetime orthodontic maximum would pay $2,500 toward a $5,000 Invisalign case — leaving $2,500 out of pocket. Orthodontic benefits are paid in installments over the course of active treatment rather than in a lump sum: the insurer typically pays a portion at the start of treatment and the remainder in equal monthly or quarterly installments as treatment progresses.

Yes — virtually all Ontario dental plans that include orthodontic benefits cover Invisalign on equal terms with traditional braces. The [Canadian Dental Association](https://www.cda-adc.ca/) codes used for comprehensive orthodontic treatment do not specify the appliance type, and insurers do not differentiate between Invisalign and braces for reimbursement purposes. If your plan covers braces, it covers Invisalign for the same amount.

The only scenario where Invisalign-specific exclusions appear is in very old legacy benefit booklets written before Invisalign became mainstream — and even these are increasingly rare. If you have any doubt, call your insurer directly and ask: does the orthodontic benefit apply equally to clear aligner treatment such as Invisalign? Get the answer in writing or reference number format.

sections.heading: What Plans Typically Do Not Cover

blocks.text: While the orthodontic benefit covers the main Invisalign treatment fee, several related costs may fall outside the benefit: the initial consultation fee (if charged separately), records fees for x-rays and digital scans, replacement aligners beyond those included in the manufacturer's replacement policy, and retainers at the end of treatment. Some plans include retainers within the orthodontic benefit; others treat them as a prosthetic and cover them under a different section; still others exclude them.

Understanding these potential gaps before treatment begins allows you to budget accurately. At our Markham clinic, the treatment coordinator prepares a written estimate showing the all-inclusive treatment fee, the expected insurance contribution based on your specific benefit, and your estimated out-of-pocket balance — before you sign any treatment agreement.

items: Lifetime orthodontic maximum — the single most important number; typically $1,500–$3,500.
Percentage covered — usually 50% of eligible fees up to the lifetime maximum.
Waiting periods — some plans have 12–24 month waits for new enrollees.
Age limits — some plans cover orthodontics only for dependents under age 18 or 21.
Retainers — check whether your plan covers retainers within the orthodontic benefit or separately.

blocks.text: Patients who have coverage under two plans — for example, their own employer plan and their spouse's employer plan — can coordinate benefits to significantly reduce out-of-pocket costs. In dual coverage, the primary plan pays first up to its lifetime maximum; the secondary plan then pays a portion of the remaining balance. Combined, dual coverage can sometimes cover 80–100 percent of Invisalign costs for patients whose plans have generous lifetime orthodontic maximums.

Our billing team is experienced in coordinating dual orthodontic coverage and will manage the submission to both insurers on your behalf. Bring benefit cards for both plans to your consultation so we can run a benefit check on both before developing your financial plan.

sections.heading: The Canadian Dental Care Plan and Orthodontics

blocks.text: The federal [Canadian Dental Care Plan](https://www.canada.ca/en/services/benefits/dental/dental-care-plan.html) is available to households with adjusted net family income below $90,000 who do not have access to private dental insurance. The CDCP covers some orthodontic services for children and youth, though the scope and fee schedule for orthodontics under this program continues to evolve. If your household qualifies for the CDCP, bring your benefit card to your consultation and we will run a benefit check to determine what is covered.

Adult orthodontics under the CDCP is more limited; coverage in this area is primarily focused on preventing functional problems rather than elective aesthetic treatment. However, cases where misalignment causes documented functional difficulty may qualify for some coverage even for adult patients. Our administrative team stays current on CDCP updates and will advise you on the latest eligibility criteria.

After applying insurance benefits, many patients still have an out-of-pocket balance ranging from $500 to $4,000+ depending on case complexity and plan generosity. Our Markham clinic offers in-office payment plans with no interest for balances paid within 12 months, and referrals to dental financing providers offering extended terms of 24–60 months. Monthly payments on a $2,500 balance over 24 months are typically around $100 — manageable alongside other household expenses.

Patients who are self-employed or who have a health spending account (HSA) through their employer can use those funds to pay for Invisalign with pre-tax money. Dental expenses not reimbursed by insurance are also eligible for the federal Medical Expense Tax Credit, which can return meaningful dollars in tax savings for patients in higher income brackets.

sections.heading: Getting Your Insurance Picture Clarified Before You Start

blocks.text: The most empowering thing you can do before beginning Invisalign is to get a pre-determination from your insurer. Our clinic submits pre-determinations on behalf of every orthodontic patient — you will receive a written response from your insurer specifying exactly what they will pay toward your treatment before we make your first aligner. This eliminates billing surprises and allows you to plan your finances with accuracy.

[Book an Invisalign consultation](/appointments) at Smile Dental Arts Centre in Markham and bring your benefit card. We will run the benefit check, show you your ClinCheck smile simulation, and give you a complete financial picture — all at the same appointment. There is no obligation to proceed, and there is no guessing.
